item.title: HCI Lab 2 — Unity Mobile Application: From Desktop to Android
item.description:
1. Introduction and Objectives Link to heading

In this laboratory, I adapted the Moving Target Challenge from HCI Lab 1 into an Android application. The original environment placed a blue spherical Agent and a red moving Target inside a bounded arena. My objective was to make the same task playable on a touchscreen, using a virtual joystick to control pursuit.

item.title: HCI Lab 3 — Building and Debugging a Local LLM Talking Character
item.description:
Introduction Link to heading

For this lab I built a local conversational character in Unity and investigated two HCI exercises: Exercise 1 — Measure Latency and Exercise 4 — Show the Thinking? The central challenge was not merely producing a response. The interface also had to communicate its state, remain usable during streaming, and distinguish a completed answer from a prematurely stopped generation. This report therefore focuses on implementation decisions, problems encountered, repairs, and the evidence used to check them. The final ten-trial study is reported as a small, exploratory case study rather than a generalizable user experiment.

item.title: HCI Lab 1 — Hugo Blog Setup and Unity ML-Agents Experiment
item.description:
1. Introduction Link to heading

This laboratory consisted of two main activities: setting up a personal academic blog using Hugo and exploring reinforcement learning with Unity ML-Agents.

The first activity focused on creating a functional website for documenting HCI coursework. The second involved configuring a Unity reinforcement learning environment, developing a new agent task, training a policy, and evaluating its performance.

item.title: HCI Homework 1
item.description:
Lecture 1: Affordances Link to heading

Good Affordance – The Login Screen in Genshin Impact Link to heading

The login screen of Genshin Impact is a good example of affordance in a digital interface. A large door is placed at the center of the screen, directly in front of the player. A door naturally suggests the action of entering or passing through it. At the same time, the text “Click to Begin” (点击进入 in the Chinese version) explicitly tells the user how to perform this action.
